question.problem:
Calculate the points where the ellipse 
$\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(y+3)^{2}}{12}=1$ intercepts the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
To calculate the $x$-intercept, we need to substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the ellipse and solve the resulting equation for $x.$ Doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(y+3)^{2}}{12} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(0+3)^{2}}{12} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{16}+\frac{9}{12} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{16}+\frac{3}{4} & =1 \\ (x-2)^{2}+12 & =16 \\ (x-2)^{2} & =4 \\ x-2 & =\pm 2 \\ x & =2\pm 2 \\ x & =0,4.\end{aligned}
$$
